MERGE.what: 5.13 says a fix branch that edits a test "is acceptable only where a finding says the test was wrong". This contradicts RT-FIX.md 7, which lets a fixer edit existing tests of any area in the direction of strength when a finding says a test is weak, and add its adopted regression test to a tool's test file (the `describe('regressions')` block). It also contradicts RT-FIX 4, where every `fixed` finding adds a permanent test. Read literally, MERGE would treat normal reproducer adoption as an out-of-bounds test edit. The rule should be: test edits only in the direction of strength or as adopted regressions, never weakening (RT-FIX 5.5, COMMON 4.4).

5.13 defines a fix branch's ownership as "the set of files its confirmed findings concern, as its report lists". The red-team round prompt (workflows/redteam-phase.js mergePrompt) passes only agent, branch, worktree, filesChanged, decisionsFragment and deviations. It carries no findings, no cluster area and no handoff, so MERGE cannot apply the 5.1 'files outside ownership' check to a fix branch. The file needs to say what MERGE uses instead: the cluster name in `fix/P{k}-<cluster>` as the area, plus the deviations RT-FIX 10 requires for files outside it.

The lockfile protocol says `npm install` runs "exactly once" and is "the only npm install you ever run". Branches merge one at a time, though, so in a stage where two or more branches each change dependencies (stage 0.2: P0-A3 site/package.json for KaTeX, P0-A6 root scripts and dependencies, P0-A2 fast-check), the lockfile can conflict on a second merge after it was already regenerated. 5.4 gives no procedure for that case (abort and route, defer regeneration to the end, or allow one regeneration per conflicting merge). 5.7 handles only the request case ('if that regeneration already ran in this run, route the request').

5.7 carries out a dependency request 'in root package.json only' but never says to regenerate the lockfile for it. The 'Carry it out by adding the exact pin ... and applying steps 2 to 4 of 5.4' sentence reads as covering only the pin-correction case. A dependency added without regeneration makes check 1 (`npm ci`) fail on an out-of-sync lockfile.

Two parts of the file disagree on what `blocked` means. In 5.3, a conflict needing a design decision on a branch the stage cannot stand without ends with `status: blocked` after `merge --abort`, and nothing says to reset `main` to the start commit. Section 10 defines `blocked` as 'when main was reset to the start commit', and the build-phase prompt says blocked means 'main at the last green commit'. 5.3 never says whether the earlier merges of the run stay on `main`, are folded and checked, or are reset away.
